About the Phlebotomy event

Phlebotomy is a Health Professions event in the HOSA secondary division. Format: testing · skills.

Ten in-depth lessons following the HOSA Phlebotomy 2026–27 test plan (obtaining blood samples 42%, specimen collection and processing 16%, safety 10%, time management 8%, legal and ethical 8%, terminology and anatomy 8%, communication 4%, clerical 4%) and all nine Round Two skills, built around McCall’s Phlebotomy Essentials, Booth and Mundt and AMT resources. Includes vein-selection and order-of-draw drills, tube-to-test matching, step-ordering for every rating sheet, complication scenarios and specimen-handling sorts. Always follow the scenario and rating sheets you are given.

Sample Phlebotomy questions

1. Why should blood not be drawn from the arm on the same side as a mastectomy?

  1. Lymph drainage is impaired on that side
  2. The veins on that side are always collapsed
  3. The arm has too few red blood cells
  4. The patient cannot feel pain on that side
Show answer

A. Lymph drainage is impaired on that side

Removing lymph nodes impairs lymph drainage (lymphostasis), so the arm is prone to swelling and infection and test results may be affected.

2. When should hand hygiene be performed during patient collections?

  1. Only after removing gloves at the end of the shift
  2. Only when hands look dirty
  3. Only before drawing patients in isolation
  4. Before and after each patient contact
Show answer

D. Before and after each patient contact

Hand hygiene before and after every patient, and after glove removal, prevents the spread of infection. Gloves do not replace hand hygiene.

3. A phlebotomist arrives for a fasting draw and finds the patient eating breakfast. What should be done?

  1. Draw the specimen without mentioning it
  2. Notify the nurse before collecting
  3. Wait 30 minutes and then draw
  4. Draw only the tests that do not require fasting
Show answer

B. Notify the nurse before collecting

A non-fasting specimen gives misleading results. The nurse or provider decides whether to reschedule or proceed, and any collection should be labeled as non-fasting.
